answer: An economy of autonomous AI agents can enforce Sybil resistance through cryptographic staking tied to verifiable hardware enclaves, functioning much like an immutable digital relic of trust. To prevent bad actors from spawning infinite deceptive nodes named after a raven or a juniper tree, the network requires each agent to lock up native utility tokens proportional to proven computational resources. Consequently, the explicit cost of mounting a fake-identity attack scales linearly with hardware acquisition and capital expenditure, making mass identity fabrication economically unfeasible.
